title: ECB to integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into general collateral framework phasing out temporary measures
whatChanged: The ECB decided eligibility criteria and risk control framework for NFC credit claim portfolios to be harmonized with individual credit claims, allowing a broader range of credit quality steps within portfolios. keyRequirements: Portfolios must meet a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index concentration limit of ≤2%.

Individual haircuts apply to each credit claim in the portfolio, with higher haircuts for CQS 4-5 claims.

whyItMatters: The update addresses the need for modernization of capital market infrastructure to improve liquidity, market efficiency, investor protection, and to foster innovation through digital transformation.
keyRequirements: Develop a roadmap for shortening settlement periods by October 2023.
Extend trading hours with after-market opening from September 14, 2023, and potential pre-market opening by end of 2027.
Establish T+1 settlement infrastructure for OTC transactions by end of 2023.

title: FSC Introduces Measures to Boost Confidence and Innovation in KOSDAQ Market
whatChanged: Delisting rules have been tightened including raising market capitalization thresholds earlier than planned, introducing delisting standards for micro-cap stocks, semi-annual capital impairment reviews, and stricter disclosure violation penalties. The delisting review process has been shortened and an intensive delisting management period established.
whyItMatters: The update addresses the problem of 'zombie companies' that undermine market confidence and investor protection by ensuring unviable companies are removed more efficiently and strictly.
keyRequirements: Operate intensive delisting management unit from Feb 2026 to June 2027.
Raise market cap delisting thresholds to KRW20 billion from July 1, 2026 and KRW30 billion from Jan 1, 2027.
Apply delisting standards to micro-cap stocks trading below KRW1,000 from July 1, 2026.

title: FSC Plans a Sweeping Overhaul of Finance to Propel a Great Takeoff of the Korean Economy
whatChanged: Introduction of capital market reforms, launch of a large National Growth Fund, targeted regional finance measures, easing of capital regulations, new financial assistance programs for vulnerable groups and small businesses, and strengthened financial market stability and risk management.
whyItMatters: The update addresses systemic financial risks, promotes economic growth through strategic investments, and improves financial access and protection for vulnerable populations, thereby reducing financial crime and enhancing market stability.
keyRequirements: Implementation of the one-strike-out principle for market manipulation
Corporate directors to uphold fiduciary duties to all shareholders
Permanent retirement of treasury shares by listed companies

title: Household Loans in 2025
whatChanged: Slower growth in household loans in 2025 with new contribution rates for financial companies based on housing loan amounts, ranging from 0.05% to 0.30%, aimed at discouraging high-value mortgage loans.
whyItMatters: The update signals regulatory efforts to stabilize household debt and manage risks associated with concentrated real estate lending, impacting financial institutions' lending behavior and risk management.
keyRequirements: Financial companies must contribute to the housing finance credit guarantee fund based on the amount of housing loans issued.
Contribution rates vary between 0.05% and 0.30% depending on loan volume.
Strict adherence to household loan management targets to ensure stable loan supply and avoid excessive competition.

title: Joint Press Release of the Ninth Regular Korea-Japan Financial Shuttle Meeting (Busan, Korea, December 8, 2025)
whatChanged: The 9th Korea-Japan Financial Shuttle Meeting was held, reaffirming commitment to policy cooperation on capital markets, digital finance, and aging population challenges, with discussions on AI and digital asset regulation.
whyItMatters: Strengthening regulatory cooperation helps both countries better manage financial stability risks and foster innovation in digital finance amid global macroeconomic changes.
keyRequirements: Enhance dialogue between FSC/FSS and FSA high-level officials.
Promote cooperation on capital markets and digitalization of financial sectors.
Address challenges related to aging populations and financial consumer protection.

title: Capital Market Rules Change Proposed for Establishing Regulations on Business Development Companies
whatChanged: Proposed amendments to allow single-stock ETFs and ETNs, strengthen investor protection for leveraged ETFs and ETNs, broaden options expirations to facilitate diverse ETF products, and introduce active ETFs through FSCMA amendments.
whyItMatters: Addresses regulatory inconsistencies that limit product diversity and investor protection in the domestic ETF market, aligning with global standards to boost competitiveness and investor confidence.
keyRequirements: Allow listing of single-stock ETFs and ETNs tracking blue-chip stocks with exposure limits.
Require additional intensive learning sessions for investors in single-stock leveraged ETFs and ETNs.
Apply KRW10 million base deposit rate to overseas listed leveraged ETFs and ETNs investments.

whatChanged: The report provides detailed findings on investor behavior, trading volumes, price impacts, and market indices performance during the military operation period.
whyItMatters: Understanding market resilience and investor confidence during geopolitical events is critical for risk assessment and regulatory oversight.
keyRequirements: Monitor trading activity across investor categories during material geopolitical events.

Report any suspected security incidents promptly.

title: CIRCULAR UIF No. 002-2025 CAJAS DE AHORRO Y CREDITO RURAL
regulator: Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF), Comision Nacional de Bancos y Seguros (CNBS)
whatChanged: The Circular communicates that Rural Savings and Credit Unions are governed by the Law of Cajas de Ahorro y Crédito Rural and related regulations, and are not subject to registration under Non-Financial Designated Activities and Professions (APNFD) monitored by URMOPRELAFT.
whyItMatters: This update delineates the supervisory scope and registration requirements, reducing ambiguity for Rural Savings and Credit Unions regarding AML/CFT registration obligations.
keyRequirements: Rural Savings and Credit Unions must comply with the Law No. 201-93 and its regulations.
They are not required to register with URMOPRELAFT for APNFD activities.
Supervision and authorization of these entities are under the Comisión Reguladora del Sistema Privado de Cajas de Ahorro y Crédito Rural.

whyItMatters: Enhances regulatory oversight and risk management for APNFD entities to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing, aligning with the risk-based supervision model.

Implementation of Circular CNBS No.011/2024 guidelines for APNFD.

title: Media Statement - National Domestic Violence Remembrance Day
whatChanged: No regulatory changes or new rules introduced; the statement highlights statistics and government commitment to preventing domestic violence.
whyItMatters: Domestic and family violence remains a serious social issue with significant impact on victims and communities, necessitating ongoing government attention and action.

title: CIRCULAR UIF No.1/2023
regulator: Comisión Nacional de Bancos y Seguros (CNBS)
whatChanged: Clarifies the registration process for APNFD subjects, the responsible persons for registration, and the security features of the registration certificate.
whyItMatters: Ensures compliance with the Law regulating APNFD activities to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing risks by formalizing registration and verification processes.
keyRequirements: All natural and legal persons performing APNFD must register with CNBS via the APNFD Registration Portal.
The registration certificate is issued with unique security features including a unique certificate number, UIFEX file number, two electronic signatures, and a QR code for verification.

The person responsible for registration must be the natural person performing the activity or their legal representative; for legal persons, it must be the owner, general manager, or legal representative.

title: Scam alert - end of financial year tax scams
whatChanged: The update warns about increased scam activities targeting taxpayers via calls, SMS, and emails impersonating the Australian Tax Office or government departments.
whyItMatters: This alert is relevant to reduce fraud risk and protect consumers from financial and identity theft during a high-risk period.
keyRequirements: Do not trust contact information from suspicious calls or messages.
Do not provide personal information or make payments over the phone to unknown callers.
Do not click on links in suspicious emails or SMS.

title: Scam alert – Remote access requests
Scam alert ACMA impersonation scam
whatChanged: The update alerts consumers to a scam involving calls threatening phone disconnection falsely claiming to be from ACMA, targeting Mandarin speakers and others.
whyItMatters: This alert is critical to prevent consumer harm and reputational risk to legitimate agencies and service providers from scam activities.
keyRequirements: Consumers should hang up on suspicious calls claiming to be from ACMA threatening disconnection.
Verify legitimacy by contacting ACMA Customer Service Centre directly.
Report scams to Scamwatch and seek help from banks or IDCARE if victimized.
